title: Multiply near round numbers: round, then compensate
explanation:
Numbers like 99, 49, or 102 sit right next to friendly round numbers. Rewrite them as round ± a little and distribute: $37\times99=37\times(100-1)=3700-37$. OpenStax shows this kind of splitting with movie tickets; if you think about the maths this way, you are using the distributive property [1].

When the two factors sit symmetrically around a round number, there's an even faster pattern. $(a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2$: to multiply conjugates, square the first term, square the last term, and write the product as a difference of squares [2]. For example $51\times49=50^2-1^2$.

Always compensate in the right direction. If you rounded a factor up, the round product is too big and you subtract the extra; if you rounded down, you add it back.
keyIdeas: Rounded up means subtract the extra; rounded down means add it back.

steps: Size check: both answers sit just below the round products 3700 and 2500, as expected.

pitfalls: Compensating in the wrong direction (adding when you rounded up).
Subtracting the wrong amount: $37\times99$ needs $-37$, not $-99$.
Using $a^2-b^2$ when the factors are not symmetric about $a$.
